claim: WSTS's Spring 2026 release puts 2025 global semiconductor sales at US$795.6 billion (+26.2%), revising the US$791.7 billion (+25.6%) that SIA first announced in February 2026.
evidence: WSTS Spring 2026 forecast summary table (2 Jun 2026): "Total World - $M 795,640 ... 26.2" (2025 column); SIA 6 Feb 2026: "global semiconductor sales hit $791.7 billion in 2025, an increase of 25.6%"

metric.name: Global semiconductor sales
metric.methodology: WSTS Spring 2026 release, 2025 actuals; revises SIA's Feb 2026 first estimate

notes: Supersedes the first-announced SIA figure in CLM-0293; same value as CLM-0030.

claim: WSTS's Spring 2026 release puts 2025 global memory sales at US$230.0 billion (+39.0%), revising the US$223.1 billion (+34.8%) that SIA first announced in February 2026.
evidence: WSTS Spring 2026 forecast summary table: "Memory 230,042 ... 39.0" (2025 column, US$M and YoY %); SIA 6 Feb 2026: "Memory products were second in terms of sales, increasing by 34.8% in 2024 [sic] to a total of $223.1 billion."

claim: SIA's 2026 State of the U.S. Semiconductor Industry report says American semiconductor companies spent US$76.8 billion on R&D in 2025, up 10.3% from US$69.6 billion in 2024.
evidence: "American semiconductor companies spent $76.8 billion on R&D in 2025, up from $69.6 billion in 2024 and representing a 10.3% increase in R&D spend." (2026 State of the U.S. Semiconductor Industry, p. 13-14, American Semiconductor Research; chart source 'SIA, 2026 Factbook')

metric.name: R&D expenditure
metric.population: R&D of U.S.-headquartered semiconductor companies as compiled by SIA
metric.methodology: SIA compilation from company 10-K/10-Q filings and SIA estimates (per 2026 Factbook chart source)

notes: Supersedes the 2024 figure in CLM-0295 as the latest year; also restates 2024 R&D at US$69.6bn vs US$70.0bn in the 2025 Factbook.

claim: Synopsys says most of its EDA licences are network licences and that EDA products are typically sold through Technology Subscription License (TSL) arrangements of generally two to three years; the time-based subscription and perpetual-licence-with-support arrangements it describes refer to its S&A (Ansys simulation and analysis) software.
evidence: "The majority of licenses to our EDA products and Ansys semiconductor products are network licenses..."; "Our S&A software solutions are offered as subscription solutions and also as perpetual licenses. Software subscription arrangements include bundles of time-based software licenses..." (Item 1); "EDA products and services are typically sold through Technology Subscription License (TSL) arrangements... generally two to three years" (MD&A)
notes: Corrects CLM-0199, which attributed the S&A subscription/perpetual wording to EDA.
